t: You're looking at the Suffragette Memorial, a sculpture in the north-west corner of Christchurch Gardens in Victoria. It takes the form of a scroll shaped like the letter S, finished in cold-cast bronze and set on a conical plinth. It was unveiled in 1970 and honours the men and women who fought for votes for women, many of whom endured violence and suffering. The sculptors were Lorne McKean and her husband Edwin Russell, both English sculptors who trained at the Royal Academy School. The architect Paul Paget devised and supervised the project.
